title: Building Offline Adventures with Local Open-Weight AI
summary: A concise record of the main engineering decisions behind Offline Adventures: a curated activity catalog, deterministic constraints, local Ollama inference, Pydantic structured output, recommendation diversity, and personalized mission twists.

content.text: Build a local-first AI activity planner for the Hacktoberfest Touch Grass challenge.
The selected architecture keeps hard constraints deterministic and uses a local open-weight model only for semantic ranking, explanations, and personalized mission twists.
How was the activity catalog designed?
An initial LLM-generated catalog experiment produced repetitive content. The final solution uses 50 curated and validated activities: 30 outdoor, 8 sheltered, and 12 indoor bridge.
How is the local model constrained?

Python filters activities by time, weather, energy, place, and group. Ollama receives only approved candidates. Pydantic validates three unique candidate IDs, natural explanations, and personalized twists.
What evidence supports the completed prototype?

The public repository includes an MIT license, reproducible setup instructions, 19 passing tests, a validated catalog, a real local-model smoke test, and a Streamlit interface that works on the local network.
